summary.headline: Exato Q1 FY27: revenue up 50% YoY, PAT up 104% YoY, order book raised to Rs 660 crore from Rs 600 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 50% YoY, EBITDA up about 82%, PBT up 102% and PAT up 104%, with margin gains attributed mainly to international business and order execution. Order book rose to Rs 660 crore after about Rs 60 crore of fresh bookings, mostly from international customers including iQor. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of at least 60-70% and profit growth of 70-80%, with ARR targeted at Rs 180-200 crore by FY27-end. The company is adding an AI infrastructure vertical, a US sales push, a potential acquisition, and an IP/platform product expected to start contributing earlier than the Q3 FY27 commitment. Absolute financial values (revenue, EBITDA, PAT in rupees) were not stated in the call.

financial_highlights.value: Up 50% YoY (absolute figure not stated in call)
Up about 82% YoY; margin expanded significantly
About Rs 30 crore executed from order book; Rs 221 crore executed up to Q4; cumulative Rs 251 crore
Rs 660 crore (Rs 600 crore at Q4); about Rs 410 crore unexecuted
About Rs 140 crore (Rs 118 crore at last call)
About 30% from maintenance, implementation and consulting

segments.name: CX and analytics / CX as a service
segments.commentary: Described as the growth engine; managed services across contact centre, workforce management, interaction analytics; BPO and IT/ITES above 70% of revenue. Management expects this vertical to remain the largest contributor.

segments.name: AI infrastructure (new vertical)
segments.commentary: Built over the last two months with HPE partnership (about two months old); not yet contributing revenue. Management expects 25-30% of FY27 contribution and margins of about 10-12% initially. Expected to start clicking within about a quarter.

segments.name: Unified communications
segments.commentary: Steady vertical; new logos include Kotak Life Insurance and Kotak Mutual Fund. Margin also expected at 10-12% in early years.

segments.name: Cloud ERP
segments.commentary: Growing at close to 20% CAGR per management; new sales team hired and a good pipeline with closures expected this quarter and later.

segments.name: IP / product (ExatoIQ, own platform)
segments.commentary: Revenue expected from this month or next; margins guided at 40-50%; two deals said to be near signing with new customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected at least 60-70%, or more; profitability growth expected above 70-80% (organic; inorganic on top).
ARR targeted at Rs 180-200 crore by end FY27, potentially more.
AI infrastructure expected to contribute 25-30% of FY27 business at 10-12% initial margins.
IP/product revenue to start this month or next, earlier than prior Q3 FY27 commitment; margins 40-50%.
Customer target of 300-500 additions in 2-3 years (organic and inorganic); longer-term aim of 400-500 customers.
Management aims for 500 crore revenue ambition and mentions 1,000 crore in three years as a wish list, not guidance.
Revenue mix for AI infrastructure deals: about 60-70% one-time and 30-40% recurring.
capex_capacity: AI-ready infrastructure practice built over two months; includes private AI, LLM in a Box, networking, observability and secure infrastructure; part of go-to-market for next three to four quarters.
24x7 delivery team already built; management plans to add manpower in the US as Chief Revenue Officer is based there.
Acquisition under evaluation to add geographic presence in APAC, UK, Middle East or US; a big-four firm is conducting due diligence; funding may be cash, equity or a mix.
Platform readiness had been expected by March 2027; now pulled forward given BPO agreements.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs 660 crore; new bookings of about Rs 60 crore mainly from international customers, including iQor (Rs 60-65 crore) as a new logo; expansion at TaskUs and Diligenta.
Two UK customers, one of which (Diligenta) contributed significantly; US, Singapore and UK named as key international contributors.
Client retention cited at 97-98%; over 150 clients; 20-plus contracts of three to five years with large customers.
Management cites TAM of USD 500-600 million for Exato currently, growing 18-20% CAGR; CX as a service plus AI as a service combined growth of 35-40% cited.
Competition: TTEC Digital in US; Big Four and large SIs (Wipro, TCS, Accenture, Infosys) seen as not competing directly in BPO-focused CX.
Partnerships: NiCE remains largest revenue contributor; upgraded to Platinum with Mitel (APAC); Acumatica upgraded to Gold; HPE and AWS added; Fortinet and amplifAI partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 growth expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects revenue growth of at least 60-70% and profit growth of 70-80% or more, citing international deals and AI infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: Customer count and inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 300-500 customers to be added in 2-3 years, organic and inorganic; four or five large customers added in Q1; five verticals planned from four; acquisition could add one or two verticals, though later said acquisition is limited to existing verticals.

qa_highlights.question: Contribution and margins of IP revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: IP revenue expected to start this month or next, with two deals close to signing; margins guided at 40-50%, from new clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is HPE partnership recurring or one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 60-70% one-time and 30-40% recurring revenue from these contracts; commercial terms say Exato owns the customer and the product comes from HPE.

qa_highlights.question: Top-five client concentration and retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Top five clients about 60% of revenue; management says contracts are non-cancellable and renewable, and client retention is 97-98%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ARR and order book be on a cumulative basis, and what is executable balance?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 251 crore executed cumulatively, leaving about Rs 410 crore unexecuted; order book up about Rs 150-180 crore since last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company tilt to services-led revenue and what headcount is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix will be heavily services but licences remain; headcount to be added cautiously with AI tools to be deployed internally; acquisition could add headcount.

risks_watch: Revenue concentration: top five clients about 60% of revenue; management says contracts are non-cancellable and renewable, but no contract tenor or renewal dates were given beyond 20-plus contracts of three to five years.
Execution of the AI infrastructure vertical (not yet contributing; expected to start clicking within about a quarter) and its lower initial margins of 10-12%, which may dilute margins.

Acquisition: under evaluation with a big-four firm doing due diligence; no target, size, valuation or funding mix confirmed; mix of cash, equity and staggered equity to the target was described as an initial thought.
IP/ExatoIQ revenue: start is expected this month or next, with two deals said to be near signing; margin guidance of 40-50% and customer names not yet disclosed.

Guidance of at least 60-70% revenue growth and 70-80% profit growth for FY27 rests on international deals and new verticals; management said some targets (500 crore, 1,000 crore in three years) are a wish list, not guidance.
Customer target of 300-500 additions in 2-3 years was not tied to a numeric timeline; client count is still described as 150-plus, so the progress will need verifying next quarter.
key_quotes: Our expectation is that revenue will grow at least 60 to 70% , or even more than that, and profitability will also be growing more than 70 to 80%.
The reason you see expansion of the order book from 600 crore to 660 crore is that we added iQor BPO as a new logo, which itself has added close to 60 to 65 crore of new business.

Rather than commenting specifically on this, because I cannot comment too much on ongoing matters, being a listed company, the way I am looking at it is that the company we want to acquire should have something we want to build.
So, approximately 30 and 30, or 25? Our focus is going to be CX; that is what creates the differentiation for us.
summary.management_tone: Confident and aggressive on growth, international expansion and new verticals, backed by named leadership hires. Cautious and evasive on specifics: target acquisition details, IP customer names and the UK customer were deferred to later calls, and absolute rupee financials were not disclosed.

adds.what: AI infrastructure vertical (AI-ready practice, HPE partnership) contributing 25-30% of FY27 business at 10-12% initial margins
Acquisition under evaluation for APAC, UK, Middle East or US presence (big-four due diligence)

growth.why: Management guided FY27 revenue growth of at least 60-70% and profit growth above 70-80%, backed by a Rs 660 crore order book (up from Rs 600 crore), 50% Q1 YoY revenue growth, and AI infrastructure and IP platform launches.
